Start from the route you already know

If math is definitely part of your route, start with the math syllabus and then move into mock tests.

If your target major is engineering, computing, medicine, or science, compare physics and chemistry before buying narrower packs.

If you are applying for a Chinese Government Scholarship undergraduate route, or your program is Chinese-taught, check the matching Professional Chinese syllabus early.

How to use the CSCA syllabus

Confirm which subject route applies to your undergraduate target first.

Read the exam format before you start collecting too many practice papers.

Use the module list in each CSCA syllabus page to build your study sequence.

Move into mock tests only after the syllabus structure already feels familiar.

Follow the next layer after the syllabus

The syllabus should reduce uncertainty, not increase it. Once the subject scope is clear, continue into subject pages, practice, and mock tests before narrower route decisions or product choices.

What does the CSCA syllabus help me do?

The CSCA syllabus helps you understand the official exam format, the topic scope for each subject, and what you should study before relying on mock tests.

Should I read the syllabus before buying a mock pack?

Yes. The syllabus tells you what the exam is designed to test. Mock packs become more valuable after the syllabus has already clarified the route and topic structure.

Does every CSCA applicant need all five syllabus pages?

No. Most students only need the syllabus pages that match their subject route and teaching language. The syllabus hub helps you identify which ones matter first.
